preamble: Loss of [t], usually in clusters or between vowels. English lost /t/ between /s/ and a following consonant (Christmas, castle); Middle Indo-Aryan Prakrits lost intervocalic t (Sanskrit gatá > gaa 'gone'); and White Hmong lost Proto-Hmong-Mien final *t, which survives only as tone (*jat > yim 'eight').

examples.note: Loss of /t/ between /s/ and a following consonant or syllabic sonorant.
Intervocalic stops were lost; Wiktionary also lists the hiatus-filling variant 𑀕𑀬 gaya.
Sauraseni has the voiced form 𑀫𑀼𑀤 muda instead.
RPA spelling; the final letter marks tone, not a consonant
